data.narrative:
Zipline, a Series G autonomous delivery company, is valued at $7.6B post-money following $600M+ in cumulative capital raised. The comparable universe consists of four private frontier-tech peers in the Drones & Autonomous sector: Nuro ($6.0B), Joby Aviation ($6.9B), Archer Aviation ($3.3B), and Elroy Air. No direct public comparables exist in this nascent category.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-Progression analysis applies a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier from Series G to the next financing round, implying $9.5B. Peer-Median triangulation across the three most comparable private and public peers yields a median valuation of $6.0B, with a range spanning $3.3B to $6.9B. The peer set reflects material heterogeneity in both stage maturity and valuation, a characteristic of early-stage autonomous systems markets.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $5.1B (low) to $10.9B (high), with a median of $7.8B. This range brackets the current $7.6B valuation near the midpoint, consistent with recent Series G pricing. Key uncertainties include the timing and regulatory pathway to commercialization across international markets, unit economics at scale, and sustained capital availability in a sector where peer funding remains episodic. The wide spread between stage-based and peer-based methods ($9.5B vs. $6.0B) reflects fundamental uncertainty around growth trajectory relative to current-stage comparables.
